coverage.r1: Whole file read in order. Latin-transliterated stretch [36:42]-[42:33] (‹...› forms; wrong/right kept in the transcript's Latin there). English-only stretches: [09:32]-[10:26] (Meet/computer logistics), [13:21]-[13:48], [16:12]-[16:57], and most of [29:33]-[31:05] (her explanation of بتأسف). Garbled/uncertain transcript lines left out: [03:31] 'تمام. مهمتي', [03:38] 'يا مهمني. بابا جان من ميرم بيته سريع', [03:45] 'يومي كان مني', [04:19] Amal 'جان ملت', [07:04] Amal 'وهلا شو بتمشي', [08:32] 'فندرة بنية', [20:54] 'لما كم يخلصوا', [32:07] 'مناسبة' (she said Perfect - surely معصبة misheard), [36:06] 'عتيته', [55:36] 'أنا بكرى'. [07:32] Amal 'خمسة' after his date line is a repeat I could not pin to a fix (pronunciation at most). S4 pronunciation left out: ثمانية/تلاتة for تمانية, اثنتين for تنتين (08:04), هواء for هوا (57:50), الله يفيكي (59:42), bin khaf/nakun vowels (39:24-39:39), and 'بس بتها' for ببسطها (32:27) which is a dropped root letter, not vocab. English drops in Arabic sentences ('understand' 13:54, 'makes me angry' 49:19, 'noodles' 06:50, 'Arabic or English letters' 15:54) were all self-fixed to Arabic within the turn, so no tier-3 rows; 'project', 'issue', 'problem', 'instead', 'apologize', 'moment', 'noodles' are not on her sheet. Comprehension misses not written as rows: 43:18 (بتخططوا, caught on repeat), 33:57 (answered for himself when she asked what SHE does), 50:18 (كان مرة؟ to إذا شفت حدا معصب). No swapped speaker labels noticed.
coverage.r2: Lesson opens with Meet audio trouble 09:32-13:48 (mostly English). Stretch 36:42-42:33 is Latin-transliterated in ‹...›; Latin kept there. 07:19 date line: Amal replied 'خمسة.' - unclear whether pronunciation or a fix, not filed. 07:45/08:04 clock answer changed after her 'لا، مش تلاتة ونص' - treated as a fact/time-zone correction, not language. 08:17 'blouze' is her word بلوزة in Latin, not English filler. 05:15 'project', 06:50 'noodles' (self-fixed to مكرونة), English 'issue' (used by Amal herself) are not on her sheet - no tier-3 rows. 14:08 يأتينا (MSA verb, echoed by her) and 59:42 الله يفيكي (dropped ع, S4) not filed. Several stutter-fragments (32:27 بتها for ببسطها, 34:03 بتأسف→بتتأسف self-fix) left out per S5. Medi Arabic turns counted by script: Medi lines containing Arabic script or ‹Latin Arabic›.

r3_note: Ruled all 26 with the transcript open. For the merger: (1) 52:12 مظلوم has two pieces - the vocab error (Farsi sense) is kept under D17 and D26 is its duplicate; the plural piece was a self-fix. (2) The apologize thread is split: D9 = the بتأسف didn't-know (t_amal 30:06), D23 = the لـ named-rule; do not merge them. (3) 36:27-42:30 is Latin transliteration, so those rows (D11, D12, D24, D25) are medium at best. (4) ASR-only tokens with Amal's approval or no signal (ماء D2, بخوفنا D13) were dropped as unverifiable. (5) D19 أزآن is kept as a listening-mode mishearing but sits on the S4 line. Noticed but NOT added (cannot be sure without the agreed list): 51:09 'سهل كمان' for 'quickly' answered by her 'Quickly. Just quickly' -> بسرعة (51:16-51:18) may be a vocab-A fix if neither reader has it; 42:53 'يخوفنا' without b- after her ممتاز.

rows.medi_said: بس إحنا بدأ...
rows.why: Subject is 'we' but he left the verb in the bare 3ms past بدأ; she supplied the 1pl ending -na.

rows.medi_said: بدأنا a marketing project who who لازم اشتغلت كتير
rows.why: Past obligation is kaan + laazem + bare present (B16/B2); he put the verb itself in the past after laazem.
rows.english: I had to work a lot

rows.medi_said: الله يوفقك.
rows.why: Reply to her يعطيكم العافية (05:39) is on her sheet: 'ya'tiki al'afyah response | Allah Y'afiki | الله يعافيكي'; he used a different formula (الله يوفقك, 'may God grant you success'); she moved to مبروك without comment. He does know the response (59:42 الله يفيكي), so a slip of formula; for her review.
rows.r3_why: Transcript token is clear and the sheet has the expected response; no signal from Amal, so vocab-B medium.

rows.medi_said: أنا صحيت على ثمانية.
rows.why: Answer to 'أي ساعة صحيت' gave bare على + number with no الساعة/el-; E2 wants el-saa3a + number (or عالتمانية with el-); Amal moved straight to 'شو شربت' so no signal; kept low because على + time is heard in speech. Best reading.
rows.r3_why: Transcript shows the bare form and no fix from Amal (06:18 changes topic); a defensible let-pass, low confidence.

rows.medi_said: مش مغني، مغـ، مغـ.
rows.why: He reached for 'cloudy' and produced مغني (singer); she supplied مغيم (sheet: the weather is cloudy | El-jaw m8ayyem | الجو مغيم).

rows.medi_said: مش مغيم، مغني is song.
rows.why: He volunteered the gloss مغني = 'song'; she corrected the meaning to 'singer' (sheet: singer | Mu8anni | مغني; song | U8niyye | أغنية) - a meaning fix on a word he asserted, separate from the 08:50 مغني-for-مغيم slip.
rows.r3_why: Real and distinct from the cloudy/singer slip at 08:50: here the error is the meaning he attached to مغني, and she fixed it out loud.

rows.medi_said: درجة حرارة.
rows.why: Idafa: the owner noun carries el- (sheet: temperature | Darjet el-7araara | درجة الحرارة); his first try الدرجة put el- on the head, the second dropped it entirely.

rows.medi_said: درجة الحرارة حوالين، تمنتاش.
rows.why: He said eighteen for eighty degrees; her echo-question made him fix it to تمانين (sheet: eighty | tamanin | تمانين).

rows.medi_said: درجة الحرارة حوالين، تمنتاش.
rows.why: Her sheet separates 'around / approximately | 7awaali | حوالي' from 'around / surrounding | 7awaalain | حوالين'; he used the spatial form for 'approximately 18'; she only queried the number (09:25 حلو، تمنتاش؟) - Levantine speakers do say حوالين for approximately, so low; for her review.
rows.r3_why: Transcript shows حوالين with no fix; the sheet explicitly distinguishes the two forms, so it belongs on her review page at low confidence.

rows.medi_said: ما زبت. زبت is... oh my God, what was زبت؟
rows.amal_said: ما زبت. It-- معنى it didn't work out.
rows.right: ما زبط = it didn't work out
rows.why: Didn't-know: he could not recall the meaning of her ما زبط, she explained it.

rows.medi_said: الـ Google Meet، بقدر، understand. بقدر، آ-آآآ، تفهم-
rows.why: Subject Google Meet is 'it/he', so the verb after بقدر must be 3ms يفهم; he used تفهم.

rows.medi_said: يفهم عربي، بس ما، آآآم، م-م-ما، ما يقدر أكتب عربي.
rows.why: Main-clause present after ما needs b- (ما بيقدر) and the dependent verb must stay 3ms (يكتب); he used 1sg أكتب; she let it pass.

rows.medi_said: هو راح، يأتي، راح ي-يأ-- ي-يأتينا- ... يأتينا، الـ ترجمة.
rows.why: MSA يأتي 'comes' used for 'it will bring us the translation'; Levantine uses جاب (sheet: bring | Jeeb | جيب; i bring | Ana bajeeb | أنا بجيب); her 14:41 يأتينا is an echo like her 14:52 ترجمة, not a fix - so B; low because she echoed it without objection. Best reading.
rows.english: It will bring us the translation.
rows.r3_why: Her line is a plain echo (she echoes ترجمة the same way 10 s later), so no signal; the wrong verb is real but only my reading - keep as vocab-B low, tier 1 since أتى/جاب are different lexical items.

rows.medi_said: الـ تاني مشكلة. No.
rows.amal_said: تاني، تاني مشكلة or المشكلة التانية
rows.why: Adjective follows the noun and both carry el- (A7); تاني also needs feminine التانية with مشكلة (A8).

rows.medi_said: إنه احنا، نكتب في، Arabic or English letters.
rows.why: After enno the b- is KEPT (B3); he dropped it (نكتب) in a plain-present statement 'the second problem is that we write...'; Amal answered مم-هم (16:11) and let it pass. Best reading.
rows.english: ...that we write in Arabic or English letters.
rows.r3_why: Transcript is clear (نكتب after إنه, no b-), the clause is plain present, and she gave no fix.

rows.medi_said: إنه احنا، نكتب في، Arabic or English letters.
rows.why: 'Write in [letters / a language]' takes بـ in Levantine (بنكتب بالعربي / بحروف إنجليزي), not في; he said في then broke into English, so the target noun never came - low; she let it pass. Best reading.
rows.english: ...we write in Arabic or English letters.
rows.r3_why: Different piece from D6 on the same line (preposition, not b-); real but the clause collapsed into English, so low.

rows.medi_said: يتعبك هذي الـ... That's been، I don't remember. أنا ما بـ-- ما، ما بتذكر، هذي الكلمة.
rows.amal_said: فترة means while, a while or period of time.
rows.why: She asked if he remembered فترة; he said he did not and she supplied the meaning - didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: So what, what makes you sad at this time?
rows.why: He glossed her بتعبك as 'makes you sad' (17:54 and again 18:35 'it made you sad'); she corrected to 'tired' and to present 'makes'.
rows.english: what tires you most these days

rows.medi_said: okay, tell me... Tell me كم مرة الجملة؟
rows.why: He wanted the sentence once more; sheet has 'how many times | Kam marra' vs 'one more time | Kaman marra'; she just repeated the sentence (my best reading).

rows.medi_said: هو، هما ما، ما، ما يخلصوا.
rows.why: Plain present after ما needs b-; she echoed يخلصوا without fixing (he later self-produced ما بيخلصوا at 22:48).

rows.medi_said: وأنا لازم كل اليوم، أطلبهم أو أطلب-- is it أطلب لهم or أطلبهم؟
rows.why: طلب takes من for the person asked (sheet: i order/request/ask for | Ana ba6lub (min)); he attached the object directly and offered لهم.
rows.english: I have to ask them all day

rows.medi_said: كام... كاملة؟
rows.why: He did not know كاملة in her الجملة كاملة; she repeated and he worked out 'complete' (sheet: whole / complete | kaamel | كامل) - didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: أنا بتعب كتير لما عيلتنا-- عيلتي، اللي، أشتغل معهم. و هو...
rows.why: Referring back to plural عيلتي / معهم he used singular هو; she supplied هما.
rows.english: my family, whom I work with, they...

rows.medi_said: أنا بتعب كتير لما عيلتنا-- عيلتي، اللي، أشتغل معهم.
rows.why: Relative clause in plain habitual present needs b- (اللي بشتغل معهم); no drop rule applies after اللي (the لما drop ended at عيلتي); she fixed only هو -> هما (22:44) and let this pass. Best reading.
rows.r3_why: Transcript shows أشتغل after اللي; the earlier لما (19:32 لما أشتغل) does not govern this clause; unfixed.

rows.medi_said: هما ما بيخلصوا اشتغلتهم.
rows.why: Verb form اشتغلت used as the noun 'their work'; the noun is شغل + هم.

rows.medi_said: شغلهم. و، لازم، لازم أطلب، أطلبهم-
rows.why: Same D2 slip repeated two minutes after the first fix: طلب من.

rows.medi_said: أطلب منهم كتير إنو، يخلص، يخلصهم؟
rows.why: Object 'it' (their work) rides on the verb as -وه; he put -هم (them) and first left the verb singular يخلص for a plural subject.

rows.medi_said: بتضل تعصب، تعصب، زمان طويل.
rows.why: 'for a long time' is لوقت طويل on her sheet (for a long time | la-wa2et taweel | لوقت طويل); he used زمان.

rows.medi_said: بتضل تعصب، تعصب، زمان طويل.
rows.amal_said: خطيبتي ما بتضل تعصب. ... So it's angry, not to get angry. It's the adjective. So what do I do to fix it?
rows.why: After بتضل 'stays' the state word is the participle معصب(ة), not the verb تعصب; she named it 'the adjective' and prompted him to fix it.

rows.medi_said: it's أنا بـ بنزبط. Is it b- بنزبطها؟
rows.why: He grabbed زبط (fix / work out) from her 'لازم نزبط' for 'I make her happy'; the verb is بسّط (sheet: it causes happiness | Byebse6 | بيبسط).

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say apologies.
rows.amal_said: بتأسف. Some people say بتأزر as well.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for 'apologize' (26:49, again 28:08); she pointed him to the WhatsApp word (29:45), he read بتأسف (30:00) and she confirmed it (30:06) and drilled the verb form أتأسف (31:18); sheet only has 'sorry | aasef | آسف'. The لـ preposition is a separate row (D23).
rows.r3_why: Clear asked-for word she supplied and confirmed; tier 0. Preposition piece split out to D23 so it is not counted twice.

rows.medi_said: إذا أناaa, بحكيلها.
rows.why: After iza the b- drops (B3/C6); she had asked for 'if I told her' and only echoed his form, so B and low.

rows.medi_said: أنا أعمل، ب- أ- أ- أعمل؟ بـ... أعمل. أعمل غلط. أنا-
rows.amal_said: أنا, I did something wrong. What's I made-
rows.why: He needed past 'I did' and gave a bare present أعمل (also with no b-); she prompted 'I did', he produced عملت, and she confirmed عملت over his خليت.

rows.medi_said: So ما, ما بتضل معصب؟
rows.why: Feminine subject خطيبتي takes the feminine adjective معصبة.

rows.medi_said: بأسف
rows.why: He built the verb from أسف as بأسف; the verb 'I apologize' is بتأسف (t-form), which she supplied after 'very close'.

rows.medi_said: لما، أتأس-- أت-- أتأسف.
rows.amal_said: And أتأسف takes لا so to her, أتأسف لها.
rows.why: She named the fixed preposition (أتأسف takes لـ -> أتأسف لها) while he was building 'she gets happy when I apologize (to her)'; he had not yet uttered a wrong preposition, so this is rule-teaching on a new verb rather than a recast of an error - medium; he then used it right (33:11 لما أتأسف لها). Kept apart from the D9 didn't-know so it is not double-counted.
rows.r3_why: A voiced named-rule moment on bucket D2 that the transcript shows; kept at medium with the caveat that no wrong preposition was actually said (teaching-shaped).

rows.medi_said: لما أنا، لما أنا بأعمل غلط، إشي غلط.
rows.why: After lamma the b- drops (B3); he kept بأعمل and she answered Mm-hmm.

rows.medi_said: إن، إنتي ما-
rows.why: Building 'she doesn't stay angry' about his fiancée he said إنتي (you-f); she recast هي and he said 'هي، sorry' (32:07); a pronoun word-swap, not an ending/prefix rule, so vocab tier 1 rather than B18 (no verb had been produced yet).
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same slip; the fix is a single substituted pronoun before any verb, so the brief's 'ending/prefix rule = grammar' test points to vocab-A tier 1.

rows.medi_said: وقت كتير.
rows.why: كتير 'a lot' for 'long'; her sheet phrase is لوقت طويل; he then parroted her لا as part of the phrase (لا، لا وقت طويل).

rows.medi_said: عتيته أنا، بنت-- بنتطلع، بنتطلع بنات أخوي-
rows.why: He used تطلع (look at) for 'we watch (babysit) my brother's girls'; she questioned it and built بندير بالنا على with him (sheet: i take care of | Ana badir baali | أنا بدير بالي).
rows.english: we watch / take care of my brother's daughters

rows.medi_said: So, is this, this is ‹dibir balak›? No.
rows.why: For 'we take care of my brother's daughters' he offered the set phrase dir baalak (2ms, sheet: take care | Deer baalak); she recast the we-form bindir and the -na ending on baal (sheet: i take care of | Ana badir baali); B18 person on the verb, A4 for the possessive ending. Latin transcript, so medium.
rows.english: We take care of (my brother's daughters).
rows.r3_why: He attempted a form and she conjugated it for the subject; a real B18 recast visible in the Latin stretch.

rows.medi_said: Wouldn't it be ‹balhom› 'cause we're watching the kids?
rows.amal_said: No, we are... Still this is part of the verb. ... ‹bindir balna›
rows.why: The ending on baal matches the subject (we), not the object; she said No and kept balna.

rows.medi_said: So is it ‹yahom›?
rows.why: The object of ndir balna comes after the fixed preposition على (37:42 'fi preposition after'); he tried the iyyaa-hom pronoun carrier; she said 3ala, and again 'Ala still' when he tried 3alayhom (38:13). Latin transcript, so medium.
rows.r3_why: Clear one-word recast of the verb's fixed preposition; D2. Medium only because the stretch is Latin transliteration.

rows.medi_said: ‹Alayhom›.
rows.why: He put a pronoun ending on على (عليهم) when the noun object بنات أخوي follows; she kept bare على.

rows.medi_said: ooh, I wanna say both of us. Do I just say ‹tinen›? Or-
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say 'both of us' and offered bare tinen; she supplied إحنا التنين (sheet: two | Tenein | تنين). Transcript in Latin here.
rows.r3_why: Same row from both readers; wrong copied as the transcript piece 'tinen' so it matches by text.

rows.medi_said: ‹Ahna il tinen›, ‹bin khaf, bin khaf min, is it ‹nakun ahel›?
rows.amal_said: Oh, here ‹hala ma btihtaj min›. ‹Bin khaf nakun›.
rows.why: خاف من takes a noun; before a verb clause the من goes and the bare verb follows (بنخاف نكون); she said 'here you don't need من'.

rows.medi_said: ‹Ana lazim, astamel il fa'il›, instead, instead is... Oh my God.
rows.amal_said: Oh, we don't know instead. No, no. ... ‹Badal›.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he searched for 'instead', she said they had not learned it and gave badal.

rows.medi_said: Is, ‹isma›.
rows.why: He asked the term for 'noun' (42:02); she hinted 'name' (42:06) and he attempted isma (اسمه, the possessed form); she recast ism (sheet: noun – nouns | Esem | اسم). He attempted the word, so a wrong-form tier 2 rather than a tier-0 didn't-know; Latin transcript, so medium.
rows.r3_why: The transcript shows an attempt (isma) followed by her one-word recast; an attempted wrong form is tier 2, not tier 0.

rows.medi_said: إحنا، إحنا بنخ-- بنخط. Ben-- it's just بنخط، right?
rows.why: He believed the verb form was بنخط; خطّط keeps its doubled root (sheet: i plan | Ana ba5a66et | أنا بخطط) - tier 2 rather than S4 because he asked whether the short form was the word.

rows.medi_said: بنخطط. اه، يكونوا أهل.
rows.why: Subject is 'we' so ykoon takes n-: نكون أهل; he used 3pl يكونوا, then يكون, before landing on نكون.

rows.medi_said: بتعصب. So in, in general, do you say الكل if I wanna say in general?
rows.amal_said: In general? لا. ... (46:19) بلاش. Sounds wrong. ... (46:42) you would say بشكل عام.
rows.why: He offered الكل, then Farsi على كلٍ, for 'in general'; she said لا (45:23), No (45:29), wavered ('I guess you could use it' 45:47), then 'بلاش. Sounds wrong' (46:19) and supplied بشكل عام (46:42). He attempted a word and she rejected it, so tier 1 explicit-no, not tier 0; medium because she wavered.
rows.r3_why: An attempted wrong word she explicitly rejected and replaced is tier 1; tier 0 is for words he never attempted.

rows.medi_said: على كلٍ شو، اه، شو، اه، بعصب، بعصب. I'm asking you.
rows.why: Turning her question on her ('I'm asking you': what makes YOU angry) he used 1sg بعصب with no من; her 47:04 من شو بتعصب؟ is her own question to him restated (answering his 'do you mean generally?'), not a recast of his line - so B, no signal; low because he was fumbling and بعصب could be a swallowed بتعصب. Best reading.
rows.english: In general, what makes you angry?
rows.r3_why: Her 47:04 line is not a fix (it re-asks him after a 40-s detour), so this is grammar-B not grammar; the person slip and missing من are visible but noisy - low.

rows.medi_said: So it has to be, has to be، اه، issue can، اه، can issue- ... So if I wanna say it has to be something really bad.
rows.amal_said: ما في can. It's it. ... لازم يكون issue، issue سيء.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he never produced Arabic, asked 'if I wanna say it has to be something really bad' (48:19) and she supplied لازم يكون issue سيء (B8 ykoon after laazem), which he repeated (48:28); no Arabic error to recast, so tier 0 asked with bucket B8 noted for the grammar tally.
rows.english: It has to be a really bad issue (for me to get angry).
rows.r3_why: He stayed in English and asked how to say it; that is a didn't-know (tier 0) not a grammar recast, but the construction is B8 so the bucket is kept on the row.

rows.medi_said: عشان، اه، بعصب
rows.why: After 3ashaan the b- drops; he asked 'عشان gets rid of be?' and she confirmed.

rows.medi_said: ولا إشي makes me angry. آآآه. ولا إشي، ولا إشي بيعص-- بعصبني
rows.why: Subject ولا إشي is 'it', so the verb takes 3ms بي-; he said 1sg بعصبني.

rows.medi_said: هي، آآآه. She doesn't get-- هي ما، ما تعصب
rows.why: Plain present after ما keeps b-: ما بتعصب.

rows.medi_said: ما-- هي ما بتعصب، آآآه، سهل كمان
rows.why: He used سهل (easy) as 'easily'; she steered him to 'quickly' and he produced بسرعة, which she accepted.
rows.english: she doesn't get angry easily / quickly either

rows.medi_said: إحنا مظلوم ... مظلومين ... مظلوم يعني، آآآه، مش صوت، آآآه، طويل، وما، ما بنعصب
rows.amal_said: Well, that's not the same meaning. هذا مش نفس المعنى بالعربي ... (52:57) Oh, a good word for this would be رايق ... (53:14) رايقين
rows.why: Farsi مظلوم 'meek / calm / unreactive' carried into Arabic, where it means 'oppressed' (53:47); she said it is not the same meaning and supplied رايق / رايقين (and said his هادي is 'quiet'). The r2 A9 reading (مظلوم -> مظلومين) is dropped: her 52:14 'بس-' is the start of her 'ليش؟' question, and he fixed the plural himself within a second (52:15) - self-fix before help.
rows.r3_why: Same moment, two different pieces: the vocab error is real and explicitly rejected; the plural piece was a self-fix before any prompt, so the final row is the vocab-A tier 1 one.

rows.medi_said: مظلوم يعني، آآآه، مش صوت، آآآه، طويل، وما، ما بنعصب، وما، آآآه-
rows.why: Defining مظلوم as 'not loud, and we don't get angry' he said صوت طويل ('long voice'); sheet: loud/high volume | Soat 3aali | صوت عالي; she was on the مظلوم meaning (52:39) and let it pass; low because the intended meaning is inferred from a halting line. Best reading.
rows.r3_why: Transcript shows طويل where عالي fits the meaning and the sheet has the exact phrase; unfixed, so vocab-B low for her review.

rows.medi_said: لما أنا لما أزآن. ... أز، أزأل. ... وي أزآن. لم، did you say أزآن؟
rows.why: She had said إذا كنت زهقان (54:21); he heard and reproduced it as the non-word أزآن (then أزأل) and asked 'did you say أزآن؟'; she said No and restored زهقان (sheet: bored | Zahqaan | زهقان). A mishearing of her spoken word reproduced aloud, so mode listening; borderline S4 (dropped ه + his usual ق->ء) - merger may treat as pronunciation.
rows.r3_why: Both readers kept it; the transcript ('did you say أزآن؟') shows a mishearing, not just a slurred ه, so it is kept as a listening-mode non-word (tier 1) with an S4 caveat in why.

rows.medi_said: زهآن. زهآن. بس، آه، لما بزهأ.
rows.why: After lamma the b- drops: لما أزهق.

rows.medi_said: أنا بكرى أو، أو. Oh, I can say ولا right؟ ولا،
rows.amal_said: أو؟ ... (56:06) ولا is used more for options يعني. Do you want this or that؟
rows.why: He had أو, then reached for ولا and asked if it works; she steered him back (أو؟) and explained ولا is for either-or options (C5). A bucket fits exactly, so grammar with signal asked rather than a tier-0 vocab row; medium because his actual production (أو) was right and the ولا was a question.
rows.r3_why: u/aw/wala is bucket C5 - the transcript shows a rule question she answered and a redirect to أو, so grammar/C5/asked, not vocab tier 0.

rows.medi_said: أغو، أغير الجو.
rows.why: Plain present 'I change' needs b-: بغير (sheet: i change scenery | Ba8ayyer jaw | بغير جو).

rows.medi_said: بغير الجو.
rows.why: The set phrase بغير جو takes no el- (sheet: Ba8ayyer jaw | بغير جو); he said الجو, she said 'No ال', and he repeated الجو at 58:26 anyway.
rows.english: I get a change of scenery
